sitedescription: From Tier-1 Support to Enterprise Systems Architect — driven by C# tooling, PowerShell automation, and infrastructure optimization.

profile.description:
Enterprise Systems Architect with over 15 years of experience in enterprise IT, specializing in software deployment, endpoint management, and automation.

My career has been built around SCCM, complemented by extensive hands-on experience in Group Policy management, OS deployment, application packaging, infrastructure administration, and .NET development.

Today, my primary focus is developing and maintaining an enterprise software ordering platform built on ASP.NET MVC, alongside managing Matrix42 Enterprise Manager and its SDK.

My strength lies in understanding how systems work beneath the surface, allowing me to troubleshoot complex issues, optimize existing solutions, and develop reliable tools and integrations.

buttons.title: About Me
buttons.description:
WELCOME TO MY PORTFOLIO
From IT Support to
Enterprise Architecture.
Infrastructure Engineering  ·  Automation  ·  Application Development
Building practical solutions. Sharing knowledge. Improving systems.

My journey into IT began with a background in mechanical engineering and a natural inclination toward logical thinking, problem-solving, and understanding how systems work. What started as a German-speaking IT support role gradually developed into a career focused on enterprise infrastructure, automation, and software development.

I have always been a self-directed learner. Much of my technical knowledge comes from studying existing solutions, learning from experienced colleagues, experimenting with new approaches, and continuously improving what I build. This is how I developed my skills in PowerShell, SQL, C#, VB.NET, and object-oriented programming, eventually progressing from modifying existing scripts to designing my own tools, frameworks, and automation solutions.

Learning, Improving, and Sharing

Throughout my career, I have followed a consistent principle: learn as much as possible, improve what can be improved, and share that knowledge with others. I have written hundreds of knowledge articles, documented technical processes, and shared scripts, tools, and solutions with colleagues to make their work easier and help teams become more independent.

I have great respect for engineers with deeper experience and expertise. Working alongside them has always motivated me to challenge myself, broaden my understanding, and become better at what I do. I believe that knowledge becomes more valuable when it is shared rather than kept to oneself.

My Approach

Whether I am troubleshooting an infrastructure issue, improving an existing automation framework, or developing a new application, I approach problems with the same mindset: understand the underlying mechanisms, identify opportunities for improvement, and create solutions that are practical, reliable, and maintainable.

I don't believe knowledge should stop with the person who developed a solution. The best solutions are those that others can understand, maintain, and build upon.

This portfolio reflects that journey, from IT support to enterprise infrastructure engineering, and showcases the tools, scripts, and solutions I have developed along the way.

description.desc: Serving as Technical Architect managing an in-house ASP.NET MVC deployment platform for a major European automotive manufacturer. Engineered direct API/SDK integrations with Matrix42 Enterprise Manager and SCCM inside Visual Studio Enterprise, enabling real-time application deployment tasks that trigger immediate endpoint agent installations—bypassing traditional SCCM/Intune polling delays while managing full-stack C# backend logic, database operations, and frontend UI.

Served as Technical Lead across enterprise accounts managing 100,000+ endpoints. Oversaw SCCM packaging, WinPE/HTA pre-PXE customization, Zero-Touch OS Deployments (ZTI), and Matrix42 Enterprise Server Manager optimization. Engineered full-stack internal platform tools using C#, ASP.NET MVC, Entity Framework, and PowerShell WPF GUIs, backed by optimized T-SQL database queries. Led agile workflows in Jira/Git, authored architecture in Confluence, and mentored cross-disciplinary teams.

Managed and optimized an entire SCCM 2012 R2 environment—including boundaries, site maintenance, CAS/Primary/Secondary server monitoring, distribution point management, and client health checks. Built LTI/ZTI Task Sequences, complex Windows 10 upgrade packages, USMT solutions, and compliance baselines. Executed Windows 10 Servicing and Office 365 client management via ADRs, while administering multi-domain Group Policies, isolated WSUS servers, and VMware/vSphere environments. Modernized software packaging with PSADT, built custom C#.NET WPF tools, and authored SSRS reports.

Served as Technical Lead supporting software distribution infrastructure, OS image deployment, and patch management across SMS 2003, SCCM 2007/2012/2012 R2, and Altiris 7.5/7.6/8.1 environments. Created captured images using Altiris Image Deployment (Symantec Ghost), optimized Group Policies and logon/startup scripts, and configured OU structures for deployment strategies. Engineered object-oriented .NET GUI applications and framework automation tools for internal and customer use, developed complex SQL queries in SSMS for reporting, and led technical client consultations.

Served as Technical Lead for Software Distribution managing multi-customer infrastructure, OS image deployment, and troubleshooting across SMS 2003, SCCM, and Altiris environments. Engineered custom capture images via Altiris, directed WSUS/SCCM patch management, and optimized GPO architecture by establishing targeted OU structures and tuning WMI queries. Modernized logon/startup scripts using VBScript and Batch to cut boot times, developed .NET GUI applications for customer frameworks, and delivered technical team trainings.

Elevated to Senior L2 Technical Lead at HP, steering support operations for key enterprise accounts including Monier and Panasonic. Specialized in deciphering systemic infrastructure issues from minimal diagnostics, handling complex escalations, and mentoring cross-functional team members.

Delivered multilingual L1/L2 technical support in German, English, and Dutch across major global client accounts, including Sybase, Innospec, Nalco, and Honeywell. Supported internal service desk operations and colleagues, managing ticket resolution and technical troubleshooting across enterprise environments.
Provided dedicated German-language Service Desk support for T-Systems Germany, handling user support, incident logging, ticket management, and initial technical triage.

dropdownItems.title: PC Information & Self-Service Support Tool
dropdownItems.description:
Conceived, proposed to management, and developed a VB.NET Windows Forms application to address a recurring challenge in enterprise IT support: incomplete technical information in incident tickets and repeated communication between users and support engineers. The application was distributed to company endpoints through SCCM and made easily accessible from the desktop and taskbar, allowing users to collect diagnostic information, resolve common issues, and access support resources without requiring technical expertise.

One-Click System Information Collection

Designed a straightforward interface that displays essential endpoint information, including computer identity, operating system details, hardware specifications, storage capacity, and network configuration. A prominent Copy Information to Clipboard button allows users to capture the collected information instantly and paste it into an incident ticket or email. This reduces repetitive information requests and gives support engineers useful troubleshooting details from the beginning of an investigation.

QuickFix: End-User Self-Service Remediation

Introduced a dedicated QuickFix tab containing automated solutions for common endpoint problems, including SAP Logon configuration issues involving SAPlogon.ini. Instead of opening a support ticket for a known, repeatable problem, users can select the relevant action and attempt to resolve the issue themselves. This approach makes frequently requested fixes more accessible and reduces unnecessary support interactions.

Software & Support Resource Integration

Added a Software tab providing convenient shortcuts to frequently used enterprise resources, including the software self-service portal and the locally installed SCCM Software Center. This gives users a central location for accessing software-related services without needing to remember separate application names or web addresses.

Automated Endpoint Diagnostics

Developed a Diagnostics tab that performs general endpoint checks and generates a text-based diagnostic report. Once the checks are complete, the report opens automatically in Notepad, allowing users to review the results or attach them to a support ticket or email. This provides support engineers with additional diagnostic information without requiring users to execute commands manually.

Enterprise Deployment & Accessibility

Packaged and distributed the application through SCCM, making it available across managed endpoints. Desktop and taskbar access, clearly separated functional tabs, and an intentionally prominent information-copying button were designed to make the application approachable for users with varying levels of technical experience.

The objective was simple: give users the tools to solve common problems themselves and provide support engineers with the information they need, without unnecessary back-and-forth communication.

Project documentation: https://peskyjim.blogspot.com/p/pc-info-tool.html

dropdownItems.title: Active Directory Search & Report Tool
dropdownItems.description:
Developed a lightweight Active Directory search and administration utility designed to simplify everyday directory lookups without requiring administrators to navigate the full Active Directory Users and Computers (ADUC) interface. The application provides a compact, customizable search environment for retrieving information about users, computers, and groups.

Flexible Active Directory Search

Supports searches across Active Directory user, computer, and group objects, allowing administrators to select the appropriate search scope. An additional filtering option helps narrow results when investigating specific accounts or directory objects.

Customizable Attribute Selection

Introduced a Column Select interface that allows administrators to choose which Active Directory attributes appear in the results. Information such as operating system, last logon timestamp, and other relevant object properties can be displayed without navigating through individual account properties. This makes it easier to focus on the information needed for a particular task.

Group Membership & Advanced Filtering

Includes group membership lookup options and secondary filtering capabilities to support more targeted directory investigations. These features help administrators locate relevant objects and examine directory relationships within a single interface.

One-Click Results Export

Search results can be copied directly to the clipboard, including column headers, making it easy to transfer directory information into support tickets, emails, documentation, or spreadsheets without manually collecting individual attributes.

A practical administrative utility focused on faster Active Directory lookups, customizable information retrieval, and reducing repetitive manual work.

Project documentation: https://peskyjim.blogspot.com/p/ad-query-tool.html

dropdownItems.title: IT - Ping & Remote Administration Tool
dropdownItems.description:
Developed a multithreaded endpoint monitoring and remote administration utility designed to simplify everyday troubleshooting for helpdesk engineers and system administrators. The application combines bulk network connectivity testing, endpoint information retrieval, and frequently used remote administration actions within a single desktop interface.

Multithreaded Connectivity Monitoring

Supports monitoring multiple computers simultaneously, using multithreaded ping operations to check network reachability without processing each endpoint sequentially. Results are displayed in a structured table showing hostnames, IP addresses, online or offline status, and fully qualified domain names (FQDNs), allowing administrators to quickly identify unreachable devices.

Endpoint Information Retrieval

Selecting a computer provides access to additional endpoint details through Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI). The information panel displays relevant system properties, including operating system version, hardware model, last logged-on user, installation date, last boot time, and available disk capacity. This helps support engineers gather useful diagnostic information without manually connecting to each device.

Integrated Remote Administration

Includes convenient quick-action buttons for common remote administration tasks. Administrators can retrieve system information using Get Info, open the selected computer's administrative C$ share, or initiate a remote PowerShell session. These shortcuts reduce repetitive manual steps and provide faster access to frequently used troubleshooting tools.

Centralized Troubleshooting Interface

Brings connectivity status, endpoint identification, system information, and remote access options together in one interface. By reducing the need to switch between command-line utilities and administrative consoles, the application makes routine endpoint investigations more efficient and easier to manage.

A lightweight troubleshooting utility that helps administrators monitor multiple endpoints, identify connectivity issues, and initiate remote support actions from a single location.

Project documentation: https://peskyjim.blogspot.com/p/ping-tool.html

dropdownItems.title: Active Directory Security Group Updater
dropdownItems.description:
Developed a bulk Active Directory security group management utility designed to simplify repetitive membership administration. Instead of manually updating individual security groups through Active Directory Users and Computers (ADUC), administrators can manage multiple user or computer objects across multiple target groups through a single desktop interface.

Bulk Membership Management

Supports adding or removing multiple Active Directory users and computers from multiple security groups in a single execution. Administrators provide the target objects and group names, select the required operation, and let the application process the requested membership changes. This reduces the repetitive steps involved in large-scale group administration.

Centralized Operation Controls

Provides dedicated controls for adding objects to groups, removing objects from groups, and clearing the current selection. Separate input lists for directory objects and target groups make it easier to prepare and review bulk membership operations before execution.

Error Handling & Execution Feedback

Includes a dedicated error reporting grid that identifies the affected object, target group, and corresponding error. This helps administrators distinguish successful operations from issues such as missing directory objects or existing group memberships, making troubleshooting more straightforward and reducing the need for manual verification.

Operational Efficiency & Consistency

Consolidates repetitive Active Directory membership changes into a consistent administrative workflow. By processing multiple objects and groups together and providing immediate execution feedback, the utility helps reduce manual effort and improves visibility during routine directory maintenance.

A practical bulk administration tool that simplifies Active Directory security group updates while providing clear feedback for individual membership operations.

Project documentation: https://peskyjim.blogspot.com/p/ad-security-group-updater.html

dropdownItems.title: Enterprise Client Support Utility
dropdownItems.description:
A custom-developed enterprise endpoint diagnostics and remediation utility, combining a graphical WPF interface with an extensive PowerShell automation engine. The interface was originally designed using Visual Studio's C# WPF tooling and adapted for PowerShell execution, integrating years of field-tested troubleshooting scripts into a centralized support platform.

  • Endpoint Health Diagnostics: Computer-name-based BASIC and FULL diagnostic modes provide system information and health checks, including disk space, DNS conflicts, WMI connectivity, and administrative share accessibility. BASIC diagnostics can be triggered directly using the Enter key.
  • Dual-Layer Status Reporting: A color-coded execution console displays detailed diagnostic results, while a dedicated visual Status Table provides immediate green/red indicators for rapid issue identification, particularly useful for first-line support personnel.
  • One-Click Remote Remediation: PowerShell-driven administrative actions encapsulate complex, multi-stage repair procedures behind simple GUI controls. Operations such as WMI repository repair, SCCM client recovery, and Windows Update remediation combine service management, execution sequencing, and necessary wait conditions into repeatable workflows.
  • Remote Administration: Integrated controls provide direct access to remote command execution, elevated system sessions, interactive PowerShell sessions, and targeted endpoint management operations.
  • Structured Data Retrieval: Dedicated Data Tables display information collected through diagnostic and administrative functions, allowing results to be copied directly into Excel for reporting or further analysis.
  • Modular Functionality: Technology-specific tabs, including SCCM management, organize specialized diagnostic and remediation scripts into focused operational workspaces.
  • Operational Engineering: Built around a continuously refined library of PowerShell scripts developed through real-world enterprise troubleshooting, standardizing complex support procedures and reducing the need for repetitive manual intervention.

Technologies: PowerShell | WPF | Visual Studio | C# WPF Designer | WMI | SCCM | Windows Endpoint Management

dropdownItems.title: StartUp / LogonScript Handler Framework
dropdownItems.description:
Originally inherited as a VBScript-based controller responsible for executing additional VBScript and batch files during user logon, this framework was progressively redesigned into a centrally managed, Active Directory-driven automation system supporting both user logon and computer startup operations.

Active Directory Group-Based Script Assignment

Introduced dynamic script targeting using Active Directory security groups. The controller searched for groups within a designated Organizational Unit (OU), checked the current user's group membership, and matched qualifying group names against script filenames stored on the NETLOGON share. Matching scripts were then executed automatically. The same mechanism was implemented for computer startup, using computer group membership instead of user membership. This eliminated the need to maintain individual script assignments and enabled centralized, group-based control over script execution.

Standardized Script Templates & Execution Logging

Developed a reusable script template for new logon and startup automation requests. Submitted scripts were incorporated into the template, which provided standardized execution logging, success or failure reporting, and runtime measurement. This ensured that independently developed scripts followed a consistent operational structure and could be monitored and troubleshot more effectively.

Centralized Execution Tracking & Performance Optimization

Implemented a master execution log that recorded which scripts ran during each logon or startup event, their individual execution times, and the total duration of the complete process. This made it possible to identify slow or failing scripts, investigate performance bottlenecks, and optimize the overall user logon and computer startup experience.

Technology Evaluation: VBScript vs. PowerShell

Evaluated a PowerShell-based implementation of the same framework but found that its initialization overhead increased execution time in this particular environment. Because minimizing logon and startup delays was a primary requirement, VBScript remained the more practical choice for the controller. This reinforced an important engineering principle: technology selection should be driven by operational requirements and measured performance, not simply by language capabilities.

The result was a maintainable, centrally controlled automation framework that improved script targeting, troubleshooting, execution visibility, and logon performance.

dropdownItems.title: Infrastructure Health Tester Tester
dropdownItems.description:
Designed a PowerShell-based infrastructure health monitoring framework to detect operational issues across interconnected enterprise systems and automatically escalate failures through the company's existing incident management infrastructure. The solution runs as a scheduled task on a Windows Server, performing connectivity checks and analyzing logs generated by an existing application environment.

Automated Infrastructure Health Checks

Implemented a monitoring approach combining basic connectivity verification between dependent systems with automated analysis of application and infrastructure logs. The framework identifies communication failures and operational errors, providing an additional layer of visibility into system health without requiring manual inspection.

WMI-Based Alerting & Automated Ticket Creation

When a monitored check detects a failure, the framework writes a corresponding error code into Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI). An existing company-wide monitoring solution collects this information and automatically generates an IT service management ticket, notifying the team responsible for the affected system. This approach integrates custom health checks with established enterprise alerting and incident management processes.

Detailed Logging & Incident Timeline Analysis

The framework includes standardized execution logging, with health information recorded at five-minute intervals. These records provide a historical view of system behavior, helping engineers identify approximately when an issue began, how long it persisted, and whether the affected components subsequently recovered. This improves troubleshooting and supports more accurate incident analysis.

Framework Design, Mentoring & Code Review

I developed the original concept and provided the reusable PowerShell framework and logging template. The monitoring logic was implemented by a junior engineer under my mentorship. Throughout development, I reviewed the implementation, provided technical guidance, and helped ensure the solution followed the intended architecture and operational requirements. This project demonstrates my approach to technical leadership: establish a clear foundation, support others in developing their skills, and maintain engineering quality through continuous collaboration.

The result was an automated monitoring and escalation framework that connected system-level diagnostics with enterprise incident management, improving operational visibility and reducing reliance on manual health checks.

dropdownItems.title: Automated SQL Reporting & HTML Email Dispatcher
dropdownItems.description:
Developed a PowerShell-based reporting tool that retrieves administrative rights and support group request data from an enterprise SQL Server database, transforms the results into formatted HTML tables, and distributes them through Microsoft Outlook. The solution automates a repetitive reporting process while keeping data extraction, presentation, and email delivery within a single workflow.

Automated SQL Data Extraction

Uses the PowerShell SQLServer module and Invoke-Sqlcmd to execute three targeted T-SQL queries against the AdminRights database. The queries retrieve daily counts of new support group configuration requests, administrative rights requests, and support group insertion requests over the previous seven days. Results are grouped by creation date and ordered chronologically to provide a clear overview of request activity.

Dynamic HTML Report Generation

A reusable PowerShell function processes the SQL results, standardizes date formatting, and converts the datasets into HTML table fragments. These fragments are inserted into a structured HTML email containing three reporting sections, consistent table styling, and an automatically generated timestamp. When a query returns no results, the corresponding section displays an informative message instead of an empty table.

Outlook COM-Based Email Delivery

Integrates with Microsoft Outlook through the Outlook.Application COM interface to create and send the completed report. The script configures the sender, recipients, subject, and HTML message body before dispatching the email through the active Outlook profile. This allows the reporting workflow to operate using the existing Outlook environment and appropriate mailbox permissions.

Reusable Reporting Architecture

Separates database queries, data transformation, HTML construction, and email delivery into clearly defined processing stages. The structure can be adapted to additional reporting requirements by modifying the SQL queries and report sections without redesigning the entire workflow.

A practical reporting solution that transforms raw SQL data into structured, readable email reports while reducing repetitive manual data collection and formatting.

buttons.title: Engineering Philosophy & Leadership
buttons.description:
ENGINEERING MINDSET
Build systems. Develop people.
Keep improving.
Curiosity  •  Ownership  •  Continuous Improvement

I believe great engineering is built on curiosity, accountability, and continuous improvement. Technical knowledge matters, but the willingness to learn, question assumptions, and take ownership of outcomes matters just as much.

Mistakes Are Opportunities to Improve

I encourage engineers to acknowledge mistakes openly, investigate their root causes, and turn lessons learned into better solutions. Stronger testing, peer reviews, proper error handling, and preventive measures are what transform an incident into lasting improvement. I believe in giving people opportunities to learn while maintaining clear expectations for reliability and accountability.

Potential Over Experience

Experience alone does not define a great engineer. I value curiosity, motivation, responsibility, and the willingness to develop. I invest in mentoring people who demonstrate potential, provide constructive feedback, and make a point of recognizing their achievements. Helping someone grow into a capable, independent engineer is one of the most rewarding parts of leadership.

Challenge My Decisions

I encourage colleagues to question my designs and technical decisions. Constructive disagreement exposes hidden assumptions, reveals potential defects, and leads to stronger solutions. I do not need people who always agree with me; I value people who make me think twice. Being confident in my expertise also means being comfortable admitting when someone else is right.

Listen First, Decide With Confidence

In technical discussions, I prefer to listen before presenting my own conclusions. Understanding different perspectives helps me evaluate the problem, recognize risks, and make informed architectural decisions. My goal is not to be the first person with an answer, but to contribute a solution that considers the bigger picture.

Reliability Is the Real Achievement

For me, successful architecture is not measured by how frequently I am called upon to resolve problems. It is measured by how reliably the environment operates, how effectively issues are prevented, and how independently the team can maintain and improve the solution.

My measure of success is not how often I'm needed to fix something, but how reliably things work without my intervention.

Ultimately, my goal is simple: build dependable systems, develop capable engineers, and create an environment where people are encouraged to learn, challenge, and improve.

buttons.title: About This Site
buttons.description:
Why I Built It

I originally created this website because I wanted something more personal than a LinkedIn profile or a traditional CV. Anyone can list technologies, certifications, and job titles. But I wanted to show what I've actually worked on, what I've learned along the way, and how I approach problems.

I'm not particularly interested in making things sound more complicated than they really are. If something works, it works. If it doesn't, well, that's usually where the interesting part begins.

A Little About Me

I'm generally a relaxed and calm person. I enjoy a good laugh, and I often use humor to lighten the mood, especially when things get stressful.

At work, I take my responsibilities seriously, but that doesn't mean everything has to be serious all the time. In my experience, people work better together when they're comfortable enough to ask questions, challenge ideas, and occasionally laugh at their own mistakes.

I've always been curious about how things work. Simply knowing which button to press has never been enough for me. I want to understand what happens behind that button, why it happens, and what I can do with that knowledge. That curiosity has taken me through quite a few different areas of IT over the years.

How This Website Works

The website itself is fairly straightforward. It's built with HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. Most of the content is stored in a separate data.json file, which keeps the information independent of the layout and makes it easier to maintain.

I also used AI assistance during development, particularly for experimenting with designs, refining CSS, and speeding up repetitive tasks. I don't see anything wrong with using tools that make development easier. What matters to me is understanding the result, being able to maintain it, and knowing how to fix it when something breaks. And yes, things did break along the way.

One Last Thing

This website isn't meant to suggest that I know everything. After more than 15 years in IT, I'm well aware that there's always something new to learn.

It's simply a collection of my experience, projects, and the things I've enjoyed working on. If you've made it this far, thanks for taking the time to look around!
